title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from neighbouring pages. The page belongs to Grothendieck's study of the 'équation des lacets', i.e. the system of equations behind the action of a Galois/Teichmüller-type group on (quotients of) the profinite modular group.
- 𝔊 is a quotient of SL(2,Z)^ ≅ Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. It has generators σ (image of S, order dividing 4) and ρ (order dividing 6), with σ^2 = ρ^3 = '-1' central.
- 𝔊' = {1,τ}·𝔊 is the corresponding quotient of GL(2,Z)^, where τ is the image of τ_∞ = diag(-1,1).
- G_{ρ,σ} is an ambient group containing 𝔊', via τ ↦ τ_B = (τ,-1) ∈ B_{ρ,σ}.

Previous page. The normalizer of L_σ = <σ> in G_{ρ,σ} is the image of N_σ = {1,τ_B}⋉Z_σ, where Z_σ is the centralizer of L_σ. The reason is that an element normalizing L_σ must send σ to σ or σ^{-1}.

This page.
1. The map N_σ → G is injective iff τ_B ∉ Z_σ. This holds iff σ ≠ σ^{-1}, iff σ^2 ≠ 1, iff '-1' ≠ 1 in 𝔊.
2. From τ_B(ρ) = σ(ρ^{-1}) he defines τ' = σ^{-1}τ ∈ 𝔊' (39). It corresponds to τ'_∞ = σ_∞^{-1}τ_∞ = -σ_∞τ_∞ = [[0,1],[1,0]] ∈ GL(2,Z).
3. Then τ'^2 = 1 and τ'ρτ'^{-1} = ρ^{-1}. In the margin he adds that also τ'(σ) = σ^{-1}.
4. So τ' normalizes L_ρ = <ρ> (a quotient of Z/6), hence normalizes its centralizer Z_ρ. He forms the semidirect product N_ρ = {1,τ'}⋉Z_ρ (41) and the canonical map i_ρ: N_ρ → G_{ρ,σ} (42).
5. The image of i_ρ is the normalizer of L_ρ, by the same argument as for σ, since ρ and ρ^{-1} are the only generators of L_ρ.
6. i_ρ is injective iff τ' ∉ Z_ρ. This holds iff ρ ≠ ρ^{-1}, iff ρ^2 ≠ 1, iff ρ ≠ -1.
7. Parenthetically he treats the degenerate case ρ = -1. Then ρ commutes with σ, so 𝔊 is abelian, a quotient of the abelianization Z/12 (ρ ↦ 2, σ ↦ 3), in fact a quotient of Z/4.
8. The margin notes that one may equally define N_σ = {1,τ'}⋉Z_σ using τ'. Then (43) gives maps δ_ρ = δ_G∘i_ρ: N_ρ → 𝔊_{ρ,σ} and δ_σ = δ_G∘i_σ: N_σ → 𝔊_{ρ,σ}, asserted to be epimorphisms ('on a fait ce qu'il fallait').

Purpose. These normalizers and the maps δ_ρ, δ_σ feed into the next page. There he describes the set of solutions (α, β, μ) of the loop equations: ξρ conjugate to ρ^μ, ησ conjugate to σ^μ, ξ = ε η l_1^ν. The conditions δ_σ(β) = 1 and δ_ρ(ατ^{ν_3(μ)}) = 1 cut out SG^#.

Nature of the page. This is bookkeeping for a GT-like (Grothendieck–Teichmüller) description of automorphisms of quotients of the profinite modular group preserving the conjugacy classes of the elliptic generators.
errors: No mathematical errors found. The matrix computation [[0,1],[-1,0]]·diag(-1,1) = [[0,1],[1,0]] is correct. So are τ'^2 = 1, τ'ρτ'^{-1} = ρ^{-1} and τ'στ'^{-1} = σ^{-1}, given τ_B(ρ) = σρ^{-1}σ^{-1} and τ_B(σ) = σ^{-1}.
The injectivity criterion implicitly uses that τ' (resp. τ_B) has order 2, so that the kernel of {1,τ'}⋉Z → G is nontrivial exactly when τ' ∈ Z. This holds by (40).
The surjectivity of δ_ρ, δ_σ in (43) is asserted without proof on this page. The target 𝔊_{ρ,σ} and the map δ_G are defined elsewhere.

ideas.what: Normalizer of a cyclic subgroup <ρ> generated by an element whose only generators are ρ^{±1}, described as the semidirect product of its centralizer with an involution inverting ρ
ideas.modern_name: N_G(<x>) = <t> ⋉ C_G(x) for an inverting involution t; dihedral-type extension of a centralizer

ideas.what: Choice of the involution τ' = σ^{-1}τ ↔ [[0,1],[1,0]] in GL(2,Z)^, which inverts both elliptic generators ρ and σ simultaneously
ideas.modern_name: orientation-reversing involution of the modular group (complex conjugation acting on PSL2(Z)), inverting S and ST
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; used in Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura-type studies of GT acting on SL2(Z)^
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (circulated manuscript) discusses GL(2,Z)^ and the 'lacets' equations; exact formula unsure

ideas.what: Injectivity criterion: the map N → G is injective iff '-1' ≠ 1 (for σ) or ρ ≠ -1 (for ρ); degenerate case gives abelian quotients of Z/12
ideas.modern_name: elementary case analysis on the quotients of SL2(Z)^ (abelianization Z/12)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine group-theoretic bookkeeping (normalizers as semidirect products with centralizers, a matrix check) inside Grothendieck's larger unpublished analysis of the loop equations for quotients of the profinite modular group. Nothing here is new or significant on its own; the larger program is partly known via La Longue Marche and later GT literature.
transcription_corrections: In (43) the first map should read δ_ρ = δ_G∘i_ρ (not λ_ρ).
The second equation labelled (40) is a repeated label in the manuscript (Grothendieck numbers both the matrix formula and τ'^2 = 1, τ'(ρ) = ρ^{-1} as (40)).
In the parenthetical: 'mais ici Z_ρ = ...' is likely 'mais ici ρ^2 = 1 donc' (degenerate case ρ = -1); the image is ambiguous.
Underbrace label under Gl(2,Z) is '≃ τ_{1,1}' or similar; uncertain reading.
